Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team at Arcwave is excited to move forward. Our procurement and legal teams reviewed the MSA + Order Form and attached a short set of redlines focused on IP and productization. High level questions: 

- We need confirmation whether Arcwave’s customer content and resulting model outputs can be used by Redwood for model training or improvements (we are asking for an opt-out).

Sarah — thanks for the clear note and the redlines. Appreciate the specificity. Quick answers up front:

- Training/data use: Redwood’s default for hosted customers is to not use customer content to train models that serve other customers without explicit opt-in. We can offer an opt-out in the Order Form and mark Arcwave as training-exempt.
- Feedback license: we can accept a narrow feedback license allowing operational telemetry and non-modeling improvements (e.g., bug fixes, infra tuning). Using Arcwave outputs to train shared models would require explicit permission.
- Productization carveout: we understand the ask — we typically grant customers rights to use outputs in their products. We’ll propose language that disclaims Redwood claims to derivative product IP generated by the customer from their outputs.

I’m looping in Laura (sales ops) to coordinate the order form edits, and I’ll pull in Legal for firm contract wording. Goal: get a blackline back to you within 48 hours.

Next steps: Laura will update the Order Form; I’ll get Legal’s suggested language and share both.

Thanks,
Ben

Laura / Ben — reviewed Arcwave’s redlines and drafted compact language that should address their concerns while protecting Redwood’s ability to run and improve operations. Key points below and redline suggestions inline (see excerpted text):

1) Training opt-out (Order Form clause) — proposed short form:
"Customer Data and Outputs. Customer may elect to exclude Customer Data and Outputs from Redwood model training and shared-model improvement by checking the ‘Training Exemption’ box in the Order Form. If elected, Redwood will not use such Customer Data or Outputs to train models that are made available to other customers. Redwood may retain aggregated, de-identified telemetry for reliability and performance monitoring only."

2) Feedback license (MSA section) — narrow operational license:
"Feedback License. Customer grants Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use anonymized telemetry and operational feedback solely to operate, maintain, and improve Redwood’s infrastructure and services; such license does not permit use of Customer Outputs to create or enhance models that are commercially available to third parties without Customer’s separate written consent."

3) Productization / derivative carveout (Order Form addendum):
"Customer Productization. Customer retains all right, title and interest in products, services or features Customer develops using Customer Outputs. Redwood disclaims ownership of Customer-developed derivative works that are created outside Redwood’s product offerings using Customer Outputs."

Risk notes: these are reasonable but set a precedent. Recommend:
- Acceptable for Hosted customers with explicit Order Form opt-out.
- For Dedicated / Private deployments we already support stronger guarantees (we can add contractual language or include KMS/HSM controls).

If you want, I’ll prepare a blackline of the MSA + Order Form with these inserts and include a short rationale memo for legal review.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
